domain: Install/upgrade/sync machinery as a manuscript-transmission channel: where lifecycle tooling itself copies, freezes, mislabels, or loses text across the Clavain/intercore/interverse fleet
axioms: The certifier and the copyist must not be the same machine: a channel that both transmits a text and attests the transmission has no witness
Copies converge toward whatever exemplar the machinery declares by constant — which may silently override the ecosystem's documented canon
A guard that reads provenance marks literally (marker greps, BEGIN/END blocks, version stamps inside the payload they vouch for) converts the safety mechanism into the freeze mechanism
Deletions and deprecations are transmissions too; machinery that cannot propagate a negative event certifies fossils as living
An index copy installed by the fleet drifts with the fleet: the concordance is itself a folio
behind=0 against the wrong exemplar is a green dashboard over a fork
primitives: exemplar declaration (plugin_repo_url constant, git archive HEAD, active agent-rig profile)
colophon / provenance marker (managed-by comment, BEGIN/END block, version stamp)
install-cache copy fleet (~/.codex clones, plugin-cache config copies, managed plugin overlays)
freshness attestation (doctor checks, version parity, behind counts)
failure_mode: Single-host probe: zklw-side mirror of the same machinery unexamined (GitHub-vs-canonical finding implies a mirror image there)
Stayed at the document/script/install layer per anti_overlap — intercore Go internals deferred to fd-kernel-contract
Verified copies and pointers on disk but did not execute any installer, doctor, or sync engine (read-only), so runtime invocation frequency is inferred
Cannot judge whether GitHub-as-exemplar is ever an intentional publish line vs an accident of a hardcoded constant
